topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture's subject and objectives before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Biological origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer development through the origins and clonal evolution of cancer-producing mutations.

topics.label: Evidence and debate about environmental cancer risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for how much environmental influences contribute to cancer.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents contribute to cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a specific example.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage that can lead to cancer.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the response and condition of exposed tissue shape tumour development, ending with a summary of the preceding carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Biomarker evidence in carcinogenicity assessment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological evidence of exposure supports the assessment of carcinogenic risks in human populations.

topics.label: Experimental tests of carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine laboratory approaches to identifying carcinogenic hazards and the limitations of their results.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This final subtopic draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their assessment.
